drafts.content: Thirty-second spot: open on an empty living room couch and a half-finished bowl of popcorn, cut to the same person walking into a warm, inviting Frame lobby, and close on a reserved seat waiting under the house lights as the Frame logo appears with the line 'Some nights are better out.'

The evidence suggests pricing is not the main obstacle; the booking flow itself has too many steps before a seat is confirmed, and frequent visitors want speed while occasional visitors want reassurance before committing. A simpler, one-page booking flow and a clearer confirmation step would be a practical first test. A result that would make me reconsider: if occasional visitors still fail to book even with a simpler flow, the obstacle is confidence, not friction.

This campaign targets occasional moviegoers who like the idea of a cinema night but rarely book. It uses a simple weekly email nudge paired with a local partnership offer, and a launch announcement plus a follow-up message for anyone who clicked but did not book. The main trade-off is reach versus message specificity; success is measured by the booking rate among people who opened the follow-up message.
